cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel, has finished it all: the house of the LORD AND his royal palace. Everything he wanted to do, he did. Me, I've never finished a single batch without eating half the dough off the spoon first.

cards.question: With the building all done, the LORD appears to Solomon. This is the first time the LORD has ever appeared to him.

cards.text: This is the second time the LORD appears to Solomon, just like back at Gibeon (1 Kings 3:5). And the LORD opens with this: “I have heard your prayer and petition before Me.”

cards.question: The LORD consecrates the temple Solomon built by putting His Name there. For how long?
The LORD also tells Solomon that His eyes and His heart will be at the temple for all time.

cards.text: Then the LORD turns to Solomon himself and drops the smallest word with the BIGGEST weight: IF. If Solomon walks with a heart of integrity and uprightness, doing all God commanded and keeping His statutes and ordinances…

cards.question: God says IF Solomon walks before Him the way someone else walked. Who is that someone?
If Solomon walks that way, God says He will establish Solomon's royal ___ over Israel forever.

cards.text: And that's not a brand new promise. God made it to David first: “You will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel.”
Then the LORD flips that IF over like a cookie on a spatula. What if Solomon or his sons turn away from following Him and don't keep His commandments?

cards.question: Besides turning away and not keeping His commandments, what else does the LORD name?

answers.text: Going off to serve other gods
Moving the ark out of the temple
Building a bigger palace for himself

cards.text: If that happens, God lays out what follows. And He starts with the land He gave Israel.

cards.question: What does the LORD say He would do with Israel and the land He gave them?

answers.text: Give half of it to Tyre

cards.question: God says even the temple He sanctified for His Name would be banished from His presence.
If Solomon or his sons turn away, how would all peoples see Israel?

cards.text: God paints the picture: this temple, a heap of rubble, and everyone who passes by is appalled and hisses. Like the whole highway slowing down to stare at a wreck.

cards.question: What do the people passing by the rubble of the temple ask?

answers.text: Why has the LORD done this
Who will build it back up
Where did all the gold go

cards.question: Others answer the people passing by the rubble. What reason do they give?

answers.text: They forsook the LORD for other gods
Their king built the temple too big
Their enemies were simply too strong

cards.question: The LORD they forsook is the God who brought their fathers out of the land of ___.

findings.problem: The identification of Solomon as king of Israel is not stated in 1 Kings 9:1. This outside Bible fact needs its own supporting reference, as the Gibeon detail receives on card 3.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The phrase "If Solomon walks that way" points back to earlier cards without explaining how Solomon is to walk. The question does not stand on its own.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question never identifies Solomon or his sons as the ones who might turn away. It depends on the preceding story card to supply who is being warned.

findings.problem: The words "they" and "their" have no antecedent in the question. The baker must rely on earlier cards to know that Israel forsook the LORD and that the fathers were Israel's fathers.
